## p217 A — Coal shortages, disarmament and transport through Czechoslovakia

**Sources on this page:** p217 A1, p217 A2, p217 A3, p217 A4, p217 A5. [Concise case study](../military/p217_A.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-p217-a-p217-a--coal-shortages-disarmament-and-transport-through-czechoslovakia"></a>


[ADFGVX Cipher](../../README.md) · [All readings](../README.md) · [Source and certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/README.md) · [Reading conventions](../../docs/reading-conventions.md)

**Record:** all five parts of message A, originated 24 November 1918 and
intercepted on 26 November.
**Result:** 1,014 source coordinates yield 507 baseline-label plaintext
positions. The first three parts need no coordinate repairs. Four
known-coordinate substitutions across the final two parts clarify the
transport and disarmament instructions. Unit numbers have a separately
documented historical interpretation; the published square is preserved.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p217-a-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the historical numeral and shared place-letter assignments:**

> An OHL und KM. Von [command designation unresolved] noch [keine]
> Nachricht. O.K. Scholtz: 16. Ldw. D. und 226. I.D., Maersche im
> Versammlungsraum. Nachhut 226. I.D. suedl. Rimnic Valcea.
>
> 11. Armee: Alpenkorps unveraendert. Am 22. wegen Kohlenmangels kein
> Abtransport. 6. R.D., Raum suedoestl. Oroshaza. [21?6 D.] in gestrigem
> Raum verblieben. A.O.K. Szolnok. 1 Batl. R.I.R. 21 im Poestyen
> eingetroffen. Verbleib der [damaged phrase] anderen Btlne unbekannt.
> Anscheinend fehlgeleitet.
>
> Cechen verweigern Aufenthalt. Wollen auch Durchfahrt nur nach
> Entwaffnung gestatten. Massow Budapest ist ersucht, letztere Fragen
> zu klaeren. OKM [damaged reference].

**Meaning:** The report locates troops withdrawing across Romania and
Hungary. Coal shortages have stopped outward transport. Some battalions
appear to have been misdirected; the Czechs refuse their stay and intend
to allow transit only after disarmament. Massow in Budapest has been asked
to clarify those questions.

The displayed numbers assume baseline `Y→1`, `J→2`, and `2→6`. The
contemporary French telegram identified below supports the 11th Army,
16th Landwehr, 226th Infantry and 6th Reserve Division identifications.
The same assignments yield *am 22* and R.I.R. 21. Several fields remain
damaged: `21?6 D` has not been replaced with an expected division number,
the number of other battalions is not asserted. The place spelling uses
the already established shared-Y interpretation described below. The certificate retains raw `KEENNE`;
the bracketed *keine* above is an editorial shortening outside the
same-length coordinate edition.

<a id="edition-cases-military-p217-a-poestyen-and-the-contested-route"></a>

### Poestyen and the contested route

The [already established DD=Y interpretation](../../experiments/p215_hungarian_y/README.md)
reads the entirely observed `POEST4EN` as **POESTYEN**, without a source
change. Its Y comes from plaintext position 57, source positions **139 and
222**. The same shared cell is supported by the separate Nagybanhegyes
field. This display applies that earlier result to the report; it adds no
new square assignment or fixed position.

A contemporary report places the town in the political circumstances of
the telegram. The [*Hamburgischer Correspondent*, 22 November 1918,
morning issue, Zweites Blatt p2 / PDF p7](https://img.sub.uni-hamburg.de/kitodo/PPN689065248_19181122/PDF/PPN689065248_19181122.pdf#page=7)
reprints a Budapest report dated 21 November, attributed to the *Pester
Lloyd*. It names **Poestyen** and describes the local Slovak council's
protest against Czech occupation, with neighboring communities already
under Czech control. The newspaper's hostile language reflects its own
political perspective.

The dispatch of 24 November then reports one battalion at Poestyen,
uncertainty about others, and demands for disarmament before transit.
The newspaper places the town in a contemporary territorial dispute; it
does not verify the battalion's arrival or the military demand.
[Source comparison and exact image provenance](../../experiments/late_place_comparison/README.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-p217-a-source-interpretation-and-credit"></a>

### Source, interpretation and credit

Printed p217 / PDF p220, heading **24 November 1918**:
`LP v NKJ (01.36 a.m., November 26th); VON UKS 2230 (11/24)
FUER LP (BSL) 5 TLE`. The original sender/recipient fields are retained.
The source is J. Rives Childs, *General Solution of the ADFGVX Cipher
System*, in the [public scan](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_JiNMck7eUvdrOTrH7fsj1Yh44t-VSC6/view).

The historical number interpretation uses document 39, printed p79 / PDF
p153, in *Documents diplomatiques français sur l'histoire du Bassin des
Carpates, 1918–1932*, vol. I (Budapest, 1993): Franchet d'Esperey's
19 November 1918 telegram reporting German formations as of 11 November.
The [provenance record](../../experiments/p170_continuation/military_context.json)
identifies its source and hash. It is contextual evidence, not a printed
key or proof of every later formation location.

The optional map clears the other potential numeral/J/Q/Y labels and
preserves one global bijection. It never assigns both baseline `Y` and
baseline `J` to 1. Baseline labels, conditional domains and all source
edits are separately recorded. Published period-key credit remains in
[data/keys.json](../../data/keys.json). This source inspection and edition
are by **icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro**. No first historical decipherment
priority is claimed.

```sh
python experiments/operational_recovery/verify.py --verify
```

See the [literal input](../../experiments/operational_recovery/inputs.json)
and [certificate](../../experiments/operational_recovery/certificates.json)
for source hashes, exact edits, domains and consistent re-encryption
witnesses. The witnesses fill unassigned key cells only to demonstrate
consistency; they are not proposed historical plaintexts.

## p217 B1 — Additional trains and divisional positions

**Sources on this page:** p217 B1. [Concise case study](../military/nov24_train_report.md).

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov24-train-report-p217-b1--additional-trains-and-divisional-positions"></a>



**Conditional recovery: icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro.** A repeated-group
model recovers the train-dispatch sentence and an Oroshaza position report.
The selected frame has **76/102 fixed raw positions**. Lexical fills reach
**96/102 with zero observed-coordinate substitutions**; a separate four-change
word edition reaches **99/102**.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov24-train-report-p217-b1"></a>

### p217 B1

**Readable German — zero-substitution lexical completion under the conditional frame; literal labels retained:**

> ABENDMEL7G. ALP KORPS 8 weitere Zuege abgerollt. JY0 ID unv?raendert. 2? RD Anfang Oroshaza. ?Y? Anfang B?KR0?SABA Z.

The intact central proposal says that further trains have departed. The later
passage places an `RD` leading element at Oroshaza. The labels `8`, `JY0`,
`2?`, `?Y?` and final `Z` are retained; no historical train count or unit
number is assigned. The question marks are unresolved positions.

The source prints 204 slots, including 21 masks. It genuinely repeats `FXXXF`
at source indices 45–49 and 50–54. The conditional frame excludes the first
copy and inserts five unknown slots before retained-stream index 12. No
cancellation mark is printed, and neither operation is an established
historical correction.

<details>
<summary>Source and cipher evidence</summary>

**Raw output — conditional 204-slot frame; all printed masks and added slots unassigned:**

```text
?BENDM?L7G?ALPXKO?PS8?E??EREZU?G?ABGERO?L?XJY0XIDU?V?RAENDE?T?2?RDANFA???R?SHAZAX?Y?X?NF?NGB?KR0?SABAZ
```

**Edited output — same conditional frame; zero observed substitutions, 16 printed-mask fills and four inserted-slot fills:**

```text
ABENDMEL7GXALPXKORPS8WEITEREZUEGEABGEROLLTXJY0XIDUNV?RAENDERTX2?RDANFANGOROSHAZAX?Y?XANFANGB?KR0?SABAZ
```

</details>

Every known half-pair of `WEITERE ZUEGE ABGEROLLT` and `RD ANFANG OROSHAZA`
agrees with those proposals. A separate, unrepaired [p217 A2 report](#edition-cases-military-p217-a)
also reads `OROSHAZA`; it supplies contextual spelling evidence, not a copy
of this message. The proposed E in `UNVERAENDERT` is excluded by the remaining
half-pair at position 52 and is therefore left unresolved above.

<a id="edition-cases-military-nov24-train-report-separately-priced-word-edition"></a>

### Separately priced word edition

**Readable German — optional four-substitution word edition; same frame and literal fields:**

> Abendmeldg. ALP KORPS 8 weitere Zuege abgerollt. JY0 ID unveraendert. 2? RD Anfang Oroshaza. ?Y? Anfang Bekescsaba Z.

<details>
<summary>Proposed text and exact labels</summary>

**Edited output — four observed-coordinate substitutions, 19 printed-mask fills and four inserted-slot fills; three positions unresolved:**

```text
ABENDMELDGXALPXKORPS8WEITEREZUEGEABGEROLLTXJY0XIDUNVERAENDERTX2?RDANFANGOROSHAZAX?Y?XANFANGBEKESCSABAZ
```

</details>

The four changes repair `ABENDMEL7G`, supply the excluded E, and propose
`BEKESCSABA` for `B?KR0?SABA`. That place reading is a same-length lexical
proposal. It is not a new global interpretation of the literal numeral label
`0`, and the primary layer retains the garbled field.

## p217 — Allied naval arrivals at Sevastopol

**Sources on this page:** p217. [Concise case study](../p217.md).

<a id="edition-cases-p217-p217--allied-naval-arrivals-at-sevastopol"></a>



**Status:** Earlier 2026 body reproduced exactly; later one-symbol 24STEN correction independently verified. **Key:** `TRUPPENVERSCHIEBUNG`.

**Earliest credited record:** [Prinz and GPT-6 Astra, 2026-09-17](https://www.prinzai.com/p/gpt-6-astra-solves-a-wwi-german-radio). **Current source and arithmetic review:** icekylinx and GPT-6 Astra Pro, 2 November 2026.

The raw body and keyword were published by Prinz with GPT-6 Astra on 17 September 2026. The version below includes Christian Horvat's 21 September correction.

<a id="edition-cases-p217-most-likely-reading"></a>

### Most likely reading

**Conditional interpretation — readable German under the recorded prior repair and digit hypothesis:**

> Ein englischer Kreuzer [einlief] Sewastopol [24.]sten. Ein Geschwader der Alliierten folgt 26.sten.

**Meaning:** A British cruiser arrived at Sevastopol on the 24th; an Allied squadron follows on the 26th.

**Notes:** `EINLIEG` is read editorially as `EINLIEF`. The date 24 combines Horvat's one-coordinate correction with the reported square assignment `AX=4`; the more conservative square leaves that digit as 4 or 8. Contemporary naval records support the 24/26 November interpretation independently. This historical corroboration does not authenticate the separately reported key manuscript.

<a id="edition-cases-p217-recomputed-reading"></a>

### Recomputed reading

Variant `horvat2026_24sten`: One known-symbol correction suggested in prior published commentary.

<details>
<summary>Recomputed earlier reading</summary>

**Recomputed prior reading — under the recorded variant and repairs:**

```text
EINENGLISCHERKREUZEREINLIEGXSEWASTOPOLX24STENXEINGESCHWADERDERXALLIIERTENFOLGT26STENX
```

</details>

<a id="edition-cases-p217-review"></a>

### Review

- The reported square fixes all 85 positions **conditional on `AX=4`**. The source-crop-conservative square leaves `AX/FF` as the coupled pair `{4,8}` and fixes 84 of 85 positions. Only `AX` occurs, at plaintext index 40; `FF` is unused.
- This conservative layer reads `S?STEN`, or `2?STEN` after Horvat's coordinate repair. The repair does not independently resolve the second digit.
- The claimed 1919 manuscript and December 9 key attribution were reported by the 2026 author. This audit verifies arithmetic and attested cells, not the unexamined manuscript provenance.
- Christian Horvat suggested the AVXFF→AVXVF correction in a 2026-09-21 comment on the September 19 follow-up article. Under the reported `AX=4` assignment, it changes `S4STEN` to `24STEN`.

<a id="edition-cases-p217-independent-historical-context"></a>

### Independent historical context

[Hopman's contemporary diary](../../data/reviews/hopman_context.json), published in an edited primary-source volume, records Canterbury at Sevastopol on November 24 and the Allied squadron on November 26. This independently corroborates the existing Prinz/Horvat interpretation alongside the British ship logs. It does not authenticate the separately reported key manuscript.

The Australian War Memorial also preserves a [24 November fleet memorandum](https://transcribe.awm.gov.au/transcription/item/rcdig0000179-4)
recording the advance ships' departure on 23 November and the main fleet's
planned departure from Constantinople on 25 November. The
[source review](../../experiments/p215_context/README.md#what-the-documents-support)
checks the original images and distinguishes these departure orders from the
diary's arrival record.
